outcome: Prevalence and severity of low back pain (LBP)
Type of anesthesia used during C-section
cohort: Women with lumbar scoliosis who had undergone anterior correction surgery and healthy women (control group)
finding: While women who underwent anterior correction surgery for lumbar scoliosis experienced a higher prevalence of low back pain compared to healthy controls, they did not have an increased risk of cesarean section or perinatal complications.
mod_finding: General anesthesia was more commonly used for C-sections in the scoliosis group compared to the control group.
birth_weight: Measured, but no specific findings reported
